title: Suki — 13yo DSH: weight loss with a good appetite
presentation: 13-year-old female neutered domestic shorthair, 800 g of weight loss over four months despite eating more than usual. The owner reports restlessness at night and occasional vomiting.

stages.title: Work the signalment
stages.briefing: Weight 3.4 kg, down from 4.2 kg. BCS 3/9. HR 220 bpm with a gallop rhythm, thyroid slip palpable on the left. Coat unkempt. Temperature 38.9°C. Blood pressure 175 mmHg systolic. No polyuria reported, water intake described as normal.
stages.prompt: Which findings steer you towards an endocrine cause rather than gut disease?

options.label: Weight loss with an increased appetite
options.detail: Catabolism outrunning intake

options.label: Palpable thyroid slip
options.detail: An enlarged thyroid lobe in the neck

options.label: Heart rate 220 bpm with a gallop rhythm
options.detail: Thyrotoxic cardiac effect

options.label: Occasional vomiting
options.detail: Common in both, discriminates nothing

options.label: Unkempt coat
options.detail: Non-specific in any chronic illness

stages.explanation: Weight loss on a good appetite narrows the field hard: the calories are going in, so they are being burned or lost. A palpable goitre with tachycardia and hypertension is hyperthyroidism until proven otherwise. Vomiting and a poor coat are true but useless here — they belong to every chronic feline illness on the differential list.

stages.title: Choose the panel
stages.briefing: The owner has agreed to bloods and a urine sample today.

options.label: Total T4
options.detail: The first-line test for the suspicion you have

options.label: Full biochemistry with urea and creatinine
options.detail: Hyperthyroidism masks concurrent kidney disease

options.label: Urinalysis with specific gravity
options.detail: Concentrating ability, protein, glucose

options.label: Haematology
options.detail: Baseline before methimazole

options.label: Blood pressure and fundic examination
options.detail: Hypertensive target-organ damage

options.label: Faecal parasitology as the first-line test
options.detail: Reasonable in a young cat with diarrhoea, not here

options.label: Insulin concentration
options.detail: No role in the work-up of feline weight loss

stages.explanation: A total T4 answers the question in most cats, but the panel around it matters as much: thyrotoxicosis raises GFR and hides chronic kidney disease that will surface the moment you treat it, so urea, creatinine and urine specific gravity have to be recorded before treatment, not after. Faecal work and insulin belong to other presentations.

stages.title: Interpret the results
stages.briefing: Total T4 96 nmol/L (ref 10–50). Urea 9.8 mmol/L (ref 5.7–12.9), creatinine 118 µmol/L (ref 71–212), USG 1.024, no glucosuria, UPC 0.3. Glucose 6.1 mmol/L. PCV 44%. Systolic blood pressure 175 mmHg, no retinal lesions.

options.label: Hyperthyroidism is confirmed biochemically
options.detail: T4 well above the reference interval

options.label: Kidney function needs rechecking after treatment
options.detail: A USG of 1.024 with a high GFR is not reassuring

options.label: Diabetes mellitus is excluded
options.detail: Normoglycaemia with no glucosuria

options.label: Hypertension needs treating in its own right
options.detail: No target-organ damage yet, but 175 mmHg with a high T4 will often fall on treatment alone

options.label: Protein-losing nephropathy is present
options.detail: A UPC of 0.3 is not proteinuria

stages.explanation: A T4 of 96 nmol/L in a cat with a goitre and a heart rate of 220 needs no confirmatory test. The subtle finding is the urine: a specific gravity of 1.024 in a cat with thyrotoxic hyperfiltration can hide stage 2 kidney disease, so the creatinine you act on is the one measured four weeks into treatment. Treating this blood pressure before the thyroid, on this reading, would be treating a number rather than a cat.

stages.title: Commit to a diagnosis
stages.briefing: T4 96 nmol/L, palpable goitre, HR 220 bpm, normoglycaemic, non-azotaemic on today’s sample.

options.label: Hyperthyroidism, with kidney disease to be re-assessed on treatment
options.detail: The whole of what these results support

options.label: Hyperthyroidism alone, kidneys normal
options.detail: Overstates what a single USG of 1.024 proves

options.label: Diabetes mellitus
options.detail: Excluded by normoglycaemia and no glucosuria

options.label: Chronic kidney disease as the primary problem
options.detail: Would not raise T4 or the appetite

options.label: Gastrointestinal lymphoma
options.detail: Possible in this age group, but it does not explain the goitre or the T4

stages.explanation: The diagnosis is hyperthyroidism, and the sentence has a second half: kidney function is unproven while GFR is being driven by thyroid hormone. Writing the diagnosis that way is what makes you recheck creatinine after four weeks of methimazole rather than discharging a cat whose azotaemia was hidden on the day you met it.
